headline: A dense urban hub with strong transit links and high property prices

tags.reason: The transport index is 80 against the Baku median of 55.5, supported by 4 metro stations and 154 bus stops.
Higher education presence is strong with 2.48 universities per 10,000 residents compared to the city median of 0.9.
Commercial real estate trades at 4,310 AZN per m² alongside 14.6 food venues per 10,000 residents versus the 11.37 median.

summary: Nərimanov is an active central district with a population density of 9,075 people per km², exceeding the Baku median of 2,890.5. Infrastructure scores are strong, showing a transport index of 80 and a healthcare index of 79, aided by 4 metro stations and 3.03 hospitals per 10,000 residents. However, affordability is restricted at an index of 21, as new flats average 2,722 AZN per m² compared to the median of 2,295 AZN per m². In the analyzed pool of 12,344 listings, 71% possess a title extract (çıxarış) and 33% qualify for a mortgage.
strengths: Public transport accessibility is superior with 4 metro stations and 46 bus lines (transport index 80; median 55.5).
Medical service density is elevated with 2.87 clinics per 10,000 residents (healthcare index 79; median 51.5).
Condition of identified roads is almost fully asphalted (99.4% paved; median 83.1%).
weaknesses: Residential purchase accessibility is significantly restricted (affordability index 21; median 50).
Local grocery supply is sparse relative to population size (6.67 groceries per 10,000 residents; median 13.41).
Kindergarten provision remains under the city norm (0.94 kindergartens per 10,000 residents; median 2.32).
best_for: Professionals relying on rapid transit, located within 0.6 km of the nearest metro station.
Buyers requiring documented legal status, with 71% of listings offering a title extract (çıxarış).
Residents prioritising medical access, served by 55 hospitals and 52 clinics.
watch_out: High acquisition costs for secondary housing at 2,550 AZN per m² versus the 2,084 AZN median.
Road data gaps, as 66.6% of road surfaces lack recorded surface classifications in OpenStreetMap.
Lower preschool coverage with only 17 kindergartens across 181,500 residents.
confidence_note: OpenStreetMap coverage is high, but the land price of 40,000 AZN per sot carries mock confidence and represents demo data. Flat and commercial figures derive from sample listing datasets of 12,344 properties.
